{
  "candidate_rtl": "module decoder_8bit
 #(
    parameter N = 8
) (
    input [N-1:0] in,
    output reg [(1<<N)-1:0] out
);
    wire [3:0] p0;
    wire [7:0] p1;
    wire [7:0] p2;
    wire [31:0] lower;
    wire [255:0] decoded;

    assign p0[0] = ~in[1] & ~in[0];
    assign p0[1] = ~in[1] &  in[0];
    assign p0[2] =  in[1] & ~in[0];
    assign p0[3] =  in[1] &  in[0];

    assign p1[0] = ~in[4] & ~in[3] & ~in[2];
    assign p1[1] = ~in[4] & ~in[3] &  in[2];
    assign p1[2] = ~in[4] &  in[3] & ~in[2];
    assign p1[3] = ~in[4] &  in[3] &  in[2];
    assign p1[4] =  in[4] & ~in[3] & ~in[2];
    assign p1[5] =  in[4] & ~in[3] &  in[2];
    assign p1[6] =  in[4] &  in[3] & ~in[2];
    assign p1[7] =  in[4] &  in[3] &  in[2];

    assign p2[0] = ~in[7] & ~in[6] & ~in[5];
    assign p2[1] = ~in[7] & ~in[6] &  in[5];
    assign p2[2] = ~in[7] &  in[6] & ~in[5];
    assign p2[3] = ~in[7] &  in[6] &  in[5];
    assign p2[4] =  in[7] & ~in[6] & ~in[5];
    assign p2[5] =  in[7] & ~in[6] &  in[5];
    assign p2[6] =  in[7] &  in[6] & ~in[5];
    assign p2[7] =  in[7] &  in[6] &  in[5];

    genvar g0, g1, g2;
    generate
        for (g1 = 0; g1 < 8; g1 = g1 + 1) begin : gen_lower_group
            for (g0 = 0; g0 < 4; g0 = g0 + 1) begin : gen_lower_bit
                assign lower[g1*4+g0] = p1[g1] & p0[g0];
            end
        end
        for (g2 = 0; g2 < 8; g2 = g2 + 1) begin : gen_upper_group
            for (g1 = 0; g1 < 8; g1 = g1 + 1) begin : gen_output_group
                assign decoded[g2*32+g1] = p2[g2] & lower[g1];
            end
        end
    endgenerate

    always @(*) begin
        out = decoded;
    end
endmodule",
  "bottleneck": "The original decomposition used 256 four-way output conjunctions, producing relatively large mapped output cones. The prior candidate reduced logic depth but exceeded the area cap because every output still combined four predecode terms.",
  "rewrite": "Use a 5-bit/3-bit hierarchical decode. The lower five input bits are formed from a shared 2-bit decoder and an 8-way 3-bit decoder, while the upper three bits use an 8-way decoder. Each output then combines two shared one-hot terms with two-input conjunctions.",
  "expected_timing_gain": "Expected to retain a shallow approximately four-level Boolean cone and improve or remain near the prior 0.82 ns result, with reduced final-cone complexity compared with four-input output conjunctions.",
  "area_or_other_cost": "The added intermediate lower[31:0] network is offset by replacing 256 four-input output combinations with shared two-input combinations. Expected mapped area is below the 2859.992960 um2 cap, with no storage, clock, or electrical-rule implications.",
  "functional_boundaries": "For fixed N=8, decoded[index] is asserted exactly when in equals index for every 8-bit binary input. Output width, parameter declaration/default, port declarations, unsignedness, combinational behavior, and all 256 output values are preserved exactly."
}
